---
title: "Add a clock"
subtitle: "Score a clock you fitted, combined, or took from a paper, exactly like a catalogue clock"
---

A clock of your own is a YAML entry and a coefficient file. Added to a run, it gets everything a
catalogue clock gets: the coverage check, the specimen check, a technical standard error, a row
in the report, and a manifest entry recording that it is yours and the SHA-256 of its file.

## 1. Write the entry

`my_clocks/mycohortclock.yaml`:

```yaml
id: mycohortclock
name: Cohort clock fitted on our blood samples
data_type: dna_methylation
tissue: [whole blood]
platform: [EPICv1]
training_target: [chronological age]
scale_type: age_years
unit: [years]
coefficients: mycohortclock.csv
reference: mycohortclock_reference.csv    # optional
```

`my_clocks/mycohortclock.csv`:

```
feature_id,coefficient
(Intercept),31.47
cg16867657,22.1
cg06639320,-14.8
```

[Build a clock](compare.qmd) and [Stack clocks](stack.qmd) write both files for you.

| Field | Why it is required |
|---|---|
| `scale_type` | Decides which arithmetic is legal: `age_years` permits acceleration, a pace or a relative score does not |
| `tissue` | Drives the check that your samples are the specimen the clock was fitted on |
| `training_target`, `unit` | What the score estimates, and in what |
| `coefficients` | One weight per feature, with an optional `(Intercept)` row |

Optional: `platform`, `reference` (a `feature_id,value` file of fill values for CpGs a dataset
lacks), `preprocess` and `postprocess` steps by the names in the registry, `citation`, `notes`.

## 2. Score it

From the command line, point `run` at the folder:

```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/work" bhagesh/falconage:1.0.0-cpu \
  run betas.csv --samples samples.csv --clocks-dir my_clocks
```

From Python or R, add it for the session:

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Python

```python
fa.add_clock("my_clocks/mycohortclock.yaml")
res = fa.score(d, clocks=["mycohortclock", "horvath2013"])
```

### R

```r
add_clock("my_clocks/mycohortclock.yaml")
res <- score(d, clocks = c("mycohortclock", "horvath2013"))
```

:::

## What is checked, and what a clock of your own does not get

The coefficient file must have two columns, unique feature ids and finite values; processing
steps must name operations FALCONAge implements; and the id may not replace a clock that ships
with the package. A clock of your own has no published calibration, so it gets no prediction
interval until you supply one, and no published reliability, so `interpretation()` says so.
